Dashlane offers robust password management with dark web monitoring, phishing alerts, and a VPN, but at a high price. Its Premium plan costs $64.99 annually, while the Friends and Family tier for 10 users is $97.49. A 14-day free trial is available, but all features except VPN are accessible during the trial. Dashlane’s passwordless login system allows PIN-based access but has security gaps, such as allowing weak PINs like 333333. A 2026 security incident exposed encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 customers, though internal systems weren’t breached. The company emphasizes zero-knowledge encryption, with vaults encrypted using user-derived master passwords. Dashlane also offers secure sharing, browser extensions for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, and Chromium browsers, and mobile apps for Android and iOS. It supports importing credentials from Bitwarden, LastPass, and CSV files. Privacy policies state no data sharing with third parties, and user data isn’t disclosed to governments without a subpoena. The review highlights Dashlane’s ease of use and feature set but notes its premium pricing compared to free alternatives like Proton Pass and NordPass.

item.title: Pinball Expo 2026 Highlights Industry Revival and Future Trends
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: The past, present, and future share a show floor at Pinball Expo 2026
Pinball Expo 2026 in Chicago showcases the industry's resurgence. Stern Pinball, controlling 90% of the market, hosts a tour of its factory where George Gomez explains the company's dominance. The expo floor highlights innovation beyond Stern's control, with hobbyist projects and open development kits gaining traction. Attendees witness both legacy machines and new licenses like Fallout. The event underscores pinball's revival, blending traditional manufacturing with grassroots creativity. Gary Stern's presence and Gomez's insights emphasize Stern's role in modern pinball while acknowledging emerging opportunities in the remaining 10% of the market.

item.title: Handy Backup Pro offers cloud backup but has usability issues
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Handy Backup Professional review: Robust backup with cloud support (and kinks)
Handy Backup Pro offers cloud backup but has usability issues. The software supports file backup, sync, disk imaging, and online storage services like Dropbox, OneDrive, and Amazon S3. However, users must run it as administrator for imaging tasks, and Google Drive access remains broken despite multiple reports. Pricing tiers range from $39 for basic backup to $487 for server versions. While praised for versatility and performance, the tool struggles with user errors, such as creating full disk images without excluding empty sectors and failing to warn about destination storage limits. The interface is criticized as unintuitive, requiring users to navigate complex menus. Despite these flaws, the 30-day trial is recommended for testing, though the software lags behind competitors like Acronis True Image and Macrium Reflect in reliability and ease of use.

item.title: Stranger Than Heaven: Like A Dragon's More Relentless Spin-Off
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Stranger Than Heaven builds its identity as Like A Dragon's more relentless spin-off
Stranger Than Heaven is the latest entry in Sega's Like A Dragon series, focusing on Makoto Daito's journey as a Japanese-American immigrant navigating early 20th-century Japan. The game spans five decades, from 1915 to 1965, detailing Daito's rise from an outcast in the U.S. to a key figure in the Tojo Clan. Unlike previous entries, it emphasizes a grounded, serious narrative with themes of racial prejudice and identity, rather than the series' usual blend of over-the-top action and humor. The combat system is more complex, featuring precise control over Daito's arms and a measured, skill-based approach akin to souls-style games. While the game's opening chapters had pacing issues and immersion-breaking elements like stunt casting, its focus on Daito's perspective as a mixed-race character and the evolving Japanese setting impressed reviewers. Stranger Than Heaven is set for release on January 17, 2027, for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

item.title: Russian drones in Ukraine use Chinese mesh networking tech
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Chinese-made mesh modems are giving Russian drones longer-range control over Ukraine
Russian drones in Ukraine use Chinese mesh networking technology. Shenzhen Xingkai Technology’s modems were found in a downed Gerbera drone, enabling long-range control. The discovery followed a 2024 attack and intensified after Russia blocked Starlink access in February 2026. Xingkai Tech supplied modems to Russian military suppliers in Alabuga for drone assembly. AMD denied selling FPGA chips to Xingkai, stating compliance with U.S. export laws. The CIA warns Gerberas could target Europe. Spain’s El Mundo reported U.S. intel suggesting Russia might launch Mediterranean drone strikes using a shadow fleet. A Lithuanian official noted drones could be hidden in shipping containers. The risk of attacks hinges on Russia’s maritime capabilities, making the use of mesh tech in drones a significant concern.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Iran Warns of Attacking Undersea Cables in Hormuz Strait
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Iran threatens to attack undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz, calls them 'legitimate new targets' in future conflict
Iran has labeled undersea fiber cables in the Strait of Hormuz as 'legitimate new targets' for future conflicts. General Hossein Mohebbi of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) stated that seven major cables, including the Asia-Africa-Europe-1 cable, pass through the strait, which connects Asia to Europe via Oman, the UAE, and Qatar. Mohebbi claimed these cables are 'new targets' in a potential 'third phase' of the conflict. Another IRGC official, Yadollah Javani, suggested Iran would retaliate by attacking cables if its infrastructure is struck. Experts, including Professor Alesso Patalano, acknowledge the threat as credible, citing past attacks like the 2022 Nord Stream 2 pipeline sabotage. An unnamed Iranian official noted Tehran had considered cutting the cables but avoided it to prevent global conflict, though it remains an option if tensions escalate with the U.S. Russia also has shown interest in undersea cables, with a Russian ship recently monitored near UK cables.

item.title: Oura Ring Adds Cardio Metrics to Compete With Wearables
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: The Oura Ring Heats Up With New Cardio Health Features
Oura Ring Gen 3 models now include Cardio Effort and automatic VO2 Max features to track cardiovascular health. Cardio Effort measures workout intensity by comparing heart rate responses to resting rates, categorizing weekly activity into Light to Reaching levels. VO2 Max estimates aerobic capacity using GPS-enabled activities, similar to Apple and Garmin. These updates aim to compete with wearables like Apple Watch and Garmin. Oura faces pressure from competitors like Signal Ring, which offers blood pressure monitoring without calibration. The company postponed its IPO in September due to market uncertainty and faces a lawsuit over accuracy claims. While new metrics extend existing data tracking, they also signal a catch-up strategy against rivals. Oura’s patented blood pressure measurement method remains unlaunched despite competition.

item.title: Utah Sues Kalshi Over Alleged Illegal Gambling Operations
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Utah Wants Millions From ‘Back-Alley Gambling Den’ Kalshi for Allegedly Running Illegal Gambling Business
Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed a lawsuit against Kalshi, its subsidiaries, and two financial firms, accusing them of violating state anti-gambling laws. The state compares Kalshi to a 'back-alley gambling den,' alleging it facilitates bets and collects fees from Utah users. Utah seeks to block the platform, enforce geolocation restrictions to prevent Utah residents from betting, and recover an estimated $30.6 million to $61.2 million in alleged illegal gambling profits. The lawsuit highlights Kalshi’s marketing as 'The First Nationwide Legal Sports Betting Platform,' despite its event contracts being contested as gambling. Kalshi faces similar lawsuits in New York, where the CFTC recently allowed continued operations. The legal dispute centers on whether prediction markets are federally regulated or subject to state gambling laws. Kalshi previously sued Utah in February 2026, but a federal judge rejected its claim that federal law shielded it from state enforcement. Kalshi has appealed, but the appeals court allowed Utah to enforce its laws. The company has not commented on the latest lawsuit.

item.title: Audiophile Headsets Not Ideal for Gaming: Comfort and Communication Matter More
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
Audiophile headsets prioritize audio fidelity, reproducing sound as recorded, but gaming headsets focus on comfort, convenience, and communication. Gaming headsets often include features like multi-device connectivity, adjustable EQ presets, and dedicated microphones for clear communication. While some audiophile headsets, like the Audeze Maxwell 2, offer gaming features, they sacrifice comfort or convenience. For example, the Maxwell 2 has large drivers for sound quality but is heavy and lacks precise positional audio for gaming. Gaming headsets like the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II and Razer BlackShark V3 Pro provide seamless device switching and advanced audio settings. Built-in chat mixing and noise cancellation are common in gaming headsets but rare in audiophile models. A good gaming mic is often essential, though some headsets, like the Razer BlackShark V2 Pro, rival standalone mics. Audiophile headsets typically require separate mics and lack gaming-specific software. While audiophile headsets excel in sound accuracy, gaming headsets better meet the needs of most gamers, balancing audio quality with practical features.

item.title: Automattic starts layoffs after board turmoil and executive exits
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures
Automattic, parent company of WordPress.com and Tumblr, has begun layoffs affecting communications, social media, and VIP enterprise teams. The cuts follow a board upheaval in September when CEO Matt Mullenweg resisted a failed attempt to oust him, leading to a complete board turnover and departures of executives including CFO Jeremy Klaperman and chief legal officer. Megan Fox, director of communications, cited her role being eliminated in her LinkedIn post. Mullenweg suggested Klaperman may have left due to being offended by the board’s decision to seek external candidates. Internal Slack messages revealed Mullenweg shared personal health details about an executive’s spouse, claiming the company failed to provide COBRA insurance, which employees found shocking. Additional layoffs in marketing and product teams have occurred. Mullenweg downplayed the layoffs as normal, focusing on PHP security issues. The company, with 1,397 staff, plans to stagger cuts to improve Q4 revenue ahead of a June debt renegotiation. A spokesperson noted the changes aim to offer better severance and time for affected employees.

item.title: Foldable Displays to Surge 44% in 2026
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Foldable displays are taking over, and research says it's the year of the wide folds
Omdia forecasts foldable display shipments will rise 44% in 2026, driven by demand for wide-screen foldables like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo. Analyst Brain Huh notes wide foldables could account for 44% of total foldable panel shipments. Samsung is expected to strengthen its market leadership, supplying displays for the Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra, which helped it gain 23% market share in Q3 despite a 20% YoY phone market decline. Apple lagged behind, partly due to the absence of a base iPhone 18 model. Omdia links the foldable growth to strong performance by Samsung and Apple, though the broader smartphone market remains weak, with Q3 marking the largest annual drop in 14 years. Rising phone prices and memory shortages are cited as factors driving consumer hesitation.

item.title: Apple Releases First Foldable iPhone Duo with Dual Displays
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Apple iPhone Duo review: A first-class foldable
Apple's first foldable iPhone, the Duo, features dual displays with a 5.4-inch OLED exterior and a 7.6-inch inner panel. The device includes a titanium chassis, a durable hinge, and IP68 water resistance. It uses Touch ID on the side instead of Face ID, offering a consistent unlock experience. The Duo weighs 254 grams, making it significantly heavier than competitors like the Galaxy Z Fold 8. While the design offers smooth transitions between screens and multitasking capabilities, many apps still need optimization for the dual-display setup. Apple has updated first-party apps like the App Store and Contacts to leverage the Duo's layout, but third-party apps like Telegram remain unoptimized. The phone's matte finish on the inner display reduces reflections and hides creases, though a small divot is visible at certain angles. Despite its strengths, the Duo's bulk and weight may affect portability and one-handed use.

item.title: Hims Launches At-Home Test for Low Testosterone
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Hims Has a Test for Low-T Beta Soyboys
Hims is launching an at-home testosterone testing service for men. The company’s Tasso device uses microneedles to collect a skin sample, which is analyzed for biomarkers including testosterone levels. A Hims provider reviews results and may prescribe hormone replacement therapy if deemed medically appropriate. Treatment options include injectables (once or twice weekly) and an oral pill (daily for up to 90 days). Hims emphasized that most men prioritize energy over muscle gains, aligning with manosphere and MAGA cultural narratives. The company also noted the military’s recent policy under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which mandates testosterone testing for male service members over 30 and offers treatment, despite medical concerns about its appropriateness. Hims warned against framing the service as gender-affirming care, as it could provoke backlash from men who view testosterone as essential to masculinity.

item.title: Web Development Is Easier Entry Point for App Builders
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: You need to learn web development before trying to build desktop or mobile apps
Web development is recommended before building desktop or mobile apps due to lower entry barriers. Starting with web apps requires only a code editor and browser, unlike mobile or desktop development, which demands heavy IDEs like Android Studio or Xcode, along with specific hardware. Mobile app distribution involves complex processes, including app store registration, developer fees, and device testing requirements. Web apps can be deployed quickly via platforms like GitHub Pages. Skills in web development transfer to native apps, as backend systems and UI design principles overlap. Tools like Electron and Tauri enable cross-platform app development using web technologies. While mobile and desktop projects require more resources and time, web development provides a foundational skill set that can be applied later. Beginners are advised to start with web development to avoid initial hurdles and build a solid foundation for future transitions.

item.title: White label gadgets are common in tech markets, often sold under different brands
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to spot a white label gadget, and why that's important
White label gadgets, produced by Asian factories and sold under different brands, are common in tech markets. Examples include Sony using Samsung and LG panels, Reebok-branded smart rings, and Motorola watches made by licensees. Zombie Brands like Kodak are repurposed for cheap products. Consumers should verify products by checking reviews, comparing specs, and noting identical listings on Amazon. Brands with strong reputations are less likely to risk their name on low-effort products. ODMs offer rapid white label services, leading to similar devices with minor tweaks. Identical specs and companion apps across multiple brands indicate white label manufacturing. While not inherently bad, these gadgets often lack quality and can mislead buyers. Consumers are advised to prioritize verified reviews and avoid suspiciously cheap options.

item.title: Ken Russell’s ‘The Devils’ Reclaimed as Masterpiece After 4K Restoration
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Ken Russell’s ‘The Devils’ Is a Towering Monument of Pure Filmmaking
Ken Russell’s ‘The Devils’ reemerged in 2026 after a 4K restoration, sparking renewed acclaim. The film, based on Aldous Huxley’s novel, follows Father Urbain Grandier’s trial for witchcraft in 17th-century Loudun, with Sister Jeanne accusing him of demonic possession. Oliver Reed’s performance as Grandier and Vanessa Redgrave’s portrayal of Jeanne are highlighted as iconic. The film blends horror, satire, and religious hypocrisy, with its grotesque imagery and dark humor earning praise as a ‘sacrament to artistry.’ Critics note its lush visuals, witty dialogue, and set designs rivaling David Lynch and Akira Kurosawa. The 2026 theatrical run, initially scheduled for one week, was extended due to demand. The film’s themes of institutional corruption and manufactured outsiders resonate with modern audiences, despite its controversial past. Its rediscovery has sparked online discussions and comparisons to modern films like Robert Eggers’ works. The restored version, released by Warner Bros. Clockwork, is celebrated for its enduring relevance and cinematic boldness.

item.title: DC's Clayface Film Explores Revenge and Body Horror
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: ‘Clayface’ Takes the Revenge Body to a Whole New Level
DC's Clayface film, directed by James Watkins, reimagines the character as a revenge-driven body horror story. The plot follows Matt Hagen, a scarred actor seeking justice after a brutal attack by crime boss Markos Szabo. Hagen undergoes experimental nanocell treatments to restore his appearance, but his face becomes unstable when he becomes emotionally agitated. The film explores themes of identity and self-acceptance through Hagen's transformation, blending visceral horror with a tragic arc. While praised for its intense visuals and performances, particularly Tom Rhys Harries, the film faces criticism for uneven visual effects and clunky dialogue. Watkins' direction focuses on a low-budget genre approach, emphasizing body horror and psychological tension. The climax delivers a gripping, if imperfect, conclusion. Clayface opens October 23.

item.title: New York’s first microdrama film festival tests vertical content’s appeal
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: New York’s first microdrama film festival searches for its audience
New York’s first microdrama film festival, Alza, held October 16–18, aimed to showcase vertical content on big screens. Founded by Pete Torres, the event featured microdramas and panels promoting vertical entertainment as a future industry standard. However, critics noted the dissonance of watching mobile-optimized content on large screens, with films like Pride and Prejudice adaptations and Eric Roberts’ Billionaire’s Broken Vow featuring jarring cuts. Platforms like Instagram and Vurt are expanding smart TV apps to retain vertical viewers, while streaming services experiment with vertical feeds. GammaTime’s Bill Block and Amy Sullivan emphasized targeting mobile-first audiences, including daytime TV viewers migrating to microdramas. Despite skepticism from creators like Salvador Paskowitz, who warned of AI’s dilution of quality, the festival highlighted human actors and traditional production methods. Block humorously suggested verticals signal the West’s decline, though he later clarified it was a joke. The industry’s rapid growth, however, faces challenges in production quality and audience engagement.
